solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Accident in pile-up — inadequate attention!

indicators.note: inadequate means falling short, so the word for the accident loses its final letter

parts.note: a shunt is a collision between vehicles, typically a rear-end bump in a pile-up

explanation.surface: A motorway pile-up blamed on a driver who was not paying enough attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inadequate' cuts the last letter from SHUNT, a British word for a minor vehicle collision.
explanation.definitionFit: Clipped military parade-ground command, short for 'Attention!', barked by a drill sergeant.

clue.text: Get very hot before coming in for drink

indicators.note: coming in tells us one piece enters the middle of the other

parts.note: to burn is to get very hot
to can mean before, as in ten to six

explanation.surface: A sweaty person, overheated, nips indoors for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' gives TO, as in telling the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Burton is a beer, named after Burton upon Trent, the English brewing town.

clue.text: Provide nasty arsenic and tea must be kept very sweet!

indicators.note: must be kept says one piece holds the other inside it
nasty signals the poison's letters are made unpleasant and jumbled

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: A poisoner's recipe: lace the tea with arsenic and sweeten it heavily to hide the taste.
explanation.walkthrough: The poisoning scene hides that 'tea' is the slang CHA, and 'nasty' scrambles the poison itself, split around it by 'must be kept'.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessively sugary, cloying; also the name of an artificial sweetener.

clue.text: A post-war screen actor's in conflict

parts.note: Richard Todd was a British film actor of the 1950s, famous for The Dam Busters; the apostrophe gives the S

explanation.surface: A film star from after the war is caught up in some dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Todd was a British film star of the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for being in disagreement or at variance with someone.

clue.text: Spreading fire — heck, get a covering cloth!

indicators.note: spreading suggests the letters fan out into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone panicking as a fire spreads, grabbing a cloth to smother it.
explanation.definitionFit: A square of fabric worn over the head or round the neck.

clue.text: An objection? When time's up it's forbidden

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means toward the top, so the letter for time climbs to the front

parts.note: taken as A
a 'but' is an objection, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: Someone raising an objection, told that once time runs out it's no longer allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: A BUT gives ABUT; 'When time's up' lifts its T to the top of this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Variant spelling of taboo: prohibited by custom or religion.

clue.text: Soup something to be thankful for? Inside you finally may get sick!

indicators.note: inside places the following pieces within the blessing word

parts.note: a boon is a blessing

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of you

parts.note: ill means sick

explanation.surface: A wry warning: the soup seems a blessing, but once it's inside you, you may feel sick.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear broth or stock, served on its own as a thin soup.

clue.text: Soldiers in back position with dull uniform finish getting new weapons

parts.note: the rear is the back position

indicators.note: in places the soldiers inside the combined letters

parts.note: a mat (matt) finish is a dull, even surface
men is a common term for soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers at the rear, kitted out in dull uniforms, are being issued fresh arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uniform' reads as clothing but belongs with 'finish': MAT, a dull even surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The process of re-equipping an army with arms; noun form matches the gerund.

clue.text: African's exclamation of surprise when reaching America

parts.note: ha is a cry of surprise
USA is the abbreviation for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A traveller from Africa exclaims in surprise on arriving in the States.
explanation.definitionFit: Member of a large West African people of northern Nigeria and Niger.

clue.text: Worm made otter sick

indicators.note: sick suggests the letters are disordered, unwell, into a new form

explanation.surface: A parasitic worm has made an otter ill.
explanation.definitionFit: A fluke, a parasitic flatworm of the class Trematoda.

clue.text: Seen as having nothing over 18?

definitions.meaning: 18 is the marzipan entry; a cake with nothing on top of its almond paste lacks icing

explanation.surface: Someone spotted as being no older than eighteen.
explanation.walkthrough: '18' looks like an age but points to the answer at 18-down; split the answer as NOT ICED.
explanation.definitionFit: Past participle meaning observed or perceived, matching 'Seen'.

clue.text: Guide wasting attendant's time

indicators.note: wasting means losing, so the attendant drops a letter

parts.note: a courtier is an attendant at a royal court

explanation.surface: A tour guide is squandering someone's time.
explanation.definitionFit: A tour guide employed by a travel company to look after holidaymakers.

clue.text: Time to get old pop singer Paul to render a poem

parts.note: Paul Anka is a Canadian pop singer from the late 1950s, known for Diana

explanation.surface: It's time for veteran crooner Paul Anka to perform some verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese verse form of 31 syllables in five lines.

clue.text: Building to secure in which tea is stacked up

indicators.note: in which says the next piece sits inside the pair before it

parts.note: to lock is to secure

indicators.note: stacked up in a down entry means written bottom to top

parts.note: a brew is a pot of tea

explanation.surface: A storeroom where tea chests are stacked high, locked up for safety.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'stacked up' means written upwards, a reversal; the tea is a brew, not chests.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall residential or office block of many storeys.

clue.text: Befuddled, can I still sparkle?

indicators.note: befuddled means confused, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A tipsy partygoer wonders whether they can still shine.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for spark: a tiny trace or flicker of something.

clue.text: Form of illumination to one side outside church hall's rear end

indicators.note: outside means one piece wraps around the others

parts.note: to right means to one side

indicators.note: rear end means the last letter of hall

explanation.surface: Lighting arranged to one side, outside the back of a church hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Light given off by a hand-held burning or battery lamp.

clue.text: Determination to get this writer's love on account of passion being endless for yesteryear's top man

parts.note: will means determination
this writer is the setter, so I AM
O is love, a nil score in tennis
for means because of

indicators.note: being endless means the word for passion loses its last letter

parts.note: anger is a passion

explanation.surface: A writer resolves to love an old leader despite an exhausted passion.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch prince who became King William III of England in 1689, a ruler of the past.

clue.text: Clay in ceremony associated with deceased

parts.note: the late means the deceased
a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: Clay used in a funeral ceremony for the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A red, iron-rich tropical soil, used for bricks and roads.

clue.text: Artist with inner energy, fellow carrying that paste

indicators.note: carrying means the fellow holds the other letters

parts.note: man means fellow

indicators.note: with inner places energy within the artist

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
zip means energy

explanation.surface: An energetic artist and a man bearing a paste.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet almond paste used to cover cakes or shape confections.

clue.text: Track that consists of din fronted by singer Johnny

indicators.note: fronted by means the din word comes after the singer

parts.note: Johnny Rotten was the singer of the Sex Pistols
a row is a noisy din

explanation.surface: A track featuring raucous noise led by punk frontman Johnny Rotten.
explanation.walkthrough: ROTTEN ROW is a riding track in London's Hyde Park.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridle path for horse-riding along the south side of a London royal park.

clue.text: Ring the female when beset by conflict

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the conflict word goes around

parts.note: war is conflict
she refers to a female

explanation.surface: A woman who is caught up in a war.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat ring of metal or rubber placed under a nut or bolt.

clue.text: Tackle publican outside front of inn

indicators.note: outside means the publican wraps around the letter

parts.note: a publican is the host of a pub

indicators.note: front of means the first letter of inn

explanation.surface: A landlord standing outside his pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting gear: tackle is a rope-and-pulley system for raising loads.

clue.text: Bring on pub drink maybe for audience

indicators.note: for audience means as the listeners hear it

parts.note: inn and juice: a pub and a drink, run together

explanation.surface: Someone ordering a drink at the pub for the people gathered there.
explanation.walkthrough: The parts said aloud, 'inn juice', echo the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring about or cause something, as labour is brought on medically.

clue.text: Look (I leer naughtily) — seductive female!

parts.note: lo means look

indicators.note: naughtily suggests misbehaving, the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A glance at a man leering naughtily at a temptress.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhine siren whose song lured boatmen to their doom.

clue.text: Most unlikely to be the sole support?

definitions.meaning: as in 'the final person to do something', the least likely
a shoemaker's foot-shaped form on which a shoe's sole is shaped

explanation.surface: Someone hardly fit to be the only breadwinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sole' reads as only, but means the bottom of a shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the least likely one, and a cobbler's block.

clue.text: Party female (beastly type) hugged by soldiers turning up

indicators.note: hugged by means the soldiers wrap around the female
turning up in an across clue reverses the soldiers' letters

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
a hind is a female deer

explanation.surface: At a party, a woman behaving like an animal is mobbed by soldiers who show up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses the American soldiers, giving SIG; the beastly female is a deer.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal name for a lively, noisy party or celebration.

clue.text: Spare fuel supplied to hospital

parts.note: gas is a fuel

explanation.surface: Extra fuel being delivered to a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: GASH is British slang for surplus or extra.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang (originally naval) for surplus or extra, left over.

clue.text: Possibly 'Attic'? Yes, that's originally what Athens was!

indicators.note: possibly signals another arrangement of the letters
originally means the first letter of that's

explanation.surface: Musing on 'Attic', the old word for Athenian, and what the city once was.
explanation.walkthrough: Attic means relating to ancient Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens in antiquity was an independent sovereign polis governing its own territory.

clue.text: Wines can produce violent impact, first to last

indicators.note: first to last means the opening letter moves to the end

parts.note: a shock is a violent impact

explanation.surface: Drinking wine can hit you hard.
explanation.definitionFit: German white wines from the Rhine, British name derived from Hochheim.
